reports.title: Norfork Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Some black bass and white bass are coming up sporadically early and late. Some big bass have spawned, some are on beds and some are in 30 feet of water on the bottom for some reason.
The crappie that I have been catching are mostly males staging for spawn in about 10 feet of water back in the creeks and have been singles.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: White River/Arkansas River fishing report
reports.text: In the Dale Bumpers White River National Wildlife Refuge, anglers are catching crappie and bass. Crappie have moved to deeper waters while the bass are moving up around the cypress.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text: Shelly Jeffrey at Lake Charles State Park (870-878-6595) said the bream and crappie are providing a lot of good action for anglers, while she heard no reports from black bass, white bass or catfish this past week. Even with cool mornings, the crappie were still biting. Jigs and worms were working best for crappie Reports were coming in for bream starting to hit redworms and jigs, and crickets were also popular.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Tailwater fishing report
reports.text: With the warmer water entering the system, this has brought up some alligator gar as well as crappie and nice sunfish.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are scattered from the shallow backs of coves to suspended in 30 feet of water. Some spawned out female crappie have already been caught, but the spawn should be in full swing this week and next.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bull Shoals Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Bass are in pre-spawn, spawn and a few are in post-spawn already.
(updated 4-18-2024) Crappie 101 Guide Service reports crappie are mostly staged on shallow brush now and the males are blackening up nicely.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cane Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Minnows have been popular for the crappie. A few largemouth bass have been caught near the camper dock as well.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: DeGray Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie have been trying to go shallow to spawn, but the yo-yo effect of falling and rising lake levels has made it difficult to stay on top of. When you find one crappie, you’ve likely found several. Black/chartreuse jigs are always a staple for crappie fishing in addition to a lip-hooked minnow. Spotted bass are all over the lake and are biting well on minnow-imitating lures like shallow-running cranbaits and even some topwater lures.
Darryl Morris of Family Fishing Trips (501-844-5418) said the crappie and black bass are in full-on spawn mode.
The largemouth bass are up spawning right now, and many on the north side of the lake are nearly finished up.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Catherine Tailwater (Below Carpenter Dam) fishing report
reports.text: April also promises the beginning of the crappie spawn which will add another quality game fish for the public to target.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are biting well on minnows and tube jigs. The crappie are up shallow and anglers are catching them best in the mornings. Black bass are fair on dark-colored soft plastic worms.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conway fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are still being caught around the Highway 89 bridge and at Gold Creek.
Bass are biting well on chatterbaits and crankbaits. The pond is more than 60 acres and has bass, crappie and bream.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hamilton fishing report
reports.text: Darryl Morris of Family Fishing Trips (501-844-5418) said the crappie and black bass are in full-on spawn mode.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Maumelle fishing report
reports.text:
The largemouth bass bite is slow. Spotted bass (Kentucky bass) also are slow.
Crappie are slow; try using jigs and minnows. Bream are slow. Try using crickets and worms. Catfish are slow. Small bream, liver and worms might get some action. (updated 4-4-2024) Fish ’N Stuff (501-834-5733) in Sherwood reports that crappie are spawning and anglers can catch them around the brush piles in 10 feet of water. Try a one-eighth-ounce jighead with a white and chartreuse Crappie Magnet.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Monticello fishing report
reports.text: A ll anglers are reminded that bass, crappie, catfish and bream fishing on the lake is strictly catch-and-release.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ouachita fishing report
reports.text:
Todd Gadberry at Mountain Harbor Resort and Spa (870-867-2191/800-832-2276 out-of-state) said black bass are good. Crappie are picking up.
Darryl Morris of Family Fishing Trips (501-844-5418) said the crappie and black bass are in full-on spawn mode.
There are still a lot of fish on the beds, so sight fishing is in full swing for bass.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Norfork Lake fishing report
reports.text: There are a lot of crappie under the shallower docks back in the creeks. Bass are coming up in the mornings making some people think the shad spawn is on. Black Bass. Walleye and Crappie are the best right now.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Spring River fishing report
reports.text: It’s a great time to chase smallmouth, but they will start spawning soon.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: White Oak Lake Area fishing report
reports.text: The fisheries team in the AGFC Camden Regional Office just wrapped up their bass surveys on the lake and said many large fish are still up shallow in the evenings. During their surveys, they pulled up a 12-lb. bass and an 8-lb. bass from the upper lake and another healthy 8 pounder from the lower lake.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bull Shoals Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Black bass are in prespawn, and overall bass fishing has been good; everyone is starting to catch them but it will definitely slow down after a cold front like we’ve had this week.
(updated 4-18-2024) Crappie 101 Guide Service reports that crappie are mostly staged on shallow brush now and the males are blackening up nicely.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are biting well on soft plastic worms and crankbaits fished around the shallow areas near the shoreline. Crappie are still slow for this time of year.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Horseshoe Lake fishing report
reports.text: The biggest story with the Crappie report is the wind. Friday, we caught crappie in 24 feet of water in the 10-14 foot range with a mixture of male and female fish. No report on largemouth bass.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Atkins fishing report
reports.text: Last Friday’s conditions were 72 degrees ambient temperature with a surface water temp of 65.1 degrees, perfect for bass and crappie fishing. The bait shop has live bait (bass, crappie, black salties, nightcrawlers, redworms, shad, crickets and more in stock, along with the latest and greatest lures.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are moving daily.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bull Shoals Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Black bass are in prespawn, and overall bass fishing has been good; everyone is starting to catch them but it will definitely slow down after a cold front like we’ve had this week.
(updated 4-11-2024) Crappie 101 Guide Service reports that crappie are mostly staged on shallow brush now and the males are blackening up nicely.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cane Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Nightcrawlers were being used at the exterior pier, and they were fishing from boats with minnows for crappie last Friday. Several anglers reported fishing with worms and minnows for crappie at the exterior pier, fishing with worms for anything that would bite, and one angler reported catching a 10-pound catfish (did not say where on the lake) and was going back to fish for anything with minnows.
Later that day, anglers were trying for crappie with nightcrawlers and still targeting any species that would go for minnows and worms. She heard reports from anglers on Sunday who reported fishing with crickets for anything, as well as some targeting crappie at the spillway with minnows and…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir fishing report
reports.text:
The lake was muddy Thursday after the rain, and it slowed the bite down a bit, but crappie are still being caught around the Highway 89 bridge and at Gold Creek.
Bass are biting well on crankbaits.
The pond is more than 60 acres and has bass, crappie and bream, and there were some rainbow trout stocked during the winter.
reports.lake: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: DeGray Lake fishing report
reports.text:
The area I was catching crappie in a few days ago, now I can see the bottom.
“ White bass and ‘ Kentuckies ’ ( spotted bass ) have started surfacing in the Shouse Ford area. They hit everything from crappie jigs and spoons, to topwaters.
“The crappie fishing is like a yo-yo right now for me.
“The open-water fishing for crappie by ’long pole-ing or sniping’ has slowed greatly.
Crappie are scattered and can be caught as shallow as 3 feet deep and as deep as 12 feet. Live bait and jigs both produce ample numbers of crappie.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Some crappie are roaming around chewing, while others are chowing down in pole timber or in brush piles.
Black bass are good super shallow out to 40 feet in guts, main lake points or secondary points, on Alabama rig, Carolina rig, jerkbaits, football heads or crankbaits, and Texas-rigged lizards. Stay around the shad and or spawning areas. Some bass now are eating topwater baits as well.
Crappie fishing has been good using a little Roadrunner or a Fin Spin in one-eighth ounce or quarter ounce. Anglers have also been catching crappie up shallow around buckbrush or on standing timber in about 15 feet of water. Water clarity up the lake is stained, but in the lower end it is really clear, they…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Largemouth bass are doing well. A 4-pound, 10-ounce bass was the Big Bass taken in last Saturday’s bass tournament.
Crappie are kind of slow, they report. A 38-pound buffalo was caught on a crappie minnow last week.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ouachita fishing report
reports.text:
Todd Gadberry at Mountain Harbor Resort and Spa (870-867-2191/800-832-2276 out-of-state) said black bass are good.
Crappie are biting fair. These fish can still be targeted on shallow structure with minnows or small jigs. Jugs and trotlines are producing quality catfish catches over main lake points with live or cut bait. Water temperature is ranging 58-62 degrees. The clarity is stained and the lake level is 575.92 feet msl. Call the Mountain Harbor fishing guides (Mike Wurm, 501-622-7717, or Chris Darby, 870-867-7822) for more information. (updated 4-11-2024) Capt. Darryl Morris of Family Fishing Trips (501-844-5418) said, “It’s that time of year again. Crappie are scattered and can be…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text:
* Largemouth bass activity has improved over the past week. Several large female bass between 6-9 pounds have been caught and released, including in local tournaments held on Millwood Lake recently. Five-inch Bass Assassin Shads, plastic lizards, Brush Hogs, tubes and spinnerbaits will draw a reaction in 2-6 feet depths.
Bill Lewis crankbaits like the MR-6, Echo 1.75 and SB-57 MDJ crankbaits were all getting random reaction bites over the past couple of weeks from these active roaming bass (and white bass, too) in the deeper sections of creek channels or drops from the flats into 8- to 12-feet structure with stumps present.
The largemouths’ reaction bites continue to be much more reliable…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Norfork Lake fishing report
reports.text: The topwater bite for stripers and bass usually starts by April 15. It is very clear near the shore and some bass are staging there. The bass bite is best right now on 3-inch creature baits on a one-eighth-ounce jighead, but Chatterbaits are also working.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are roaming, holding to pole timber or in brush piles, in all places they are suspended. Black bass are good. A few topwater bass also have been found.
(updated 4-11-2024) Fish ’N Stuff (501-834-5733) in Sherwood says both the bass fishing and crappie fishing have been very good in the past week. Anglers are using various approaches for bass – a Carolina rig and a jig are both being favored.
Crappie fishing has been good using a little Roadrunner or a Fin Spin in one-eighth ounce or quarter ounce. Anglers have also been catching crappie up shallow around buckbrush or on standing timber in about 15 feet of water. Water clarity up the lake is stained, but in the lower end it is really…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Poinsett fishing report
reports.text: Numerous anglers have reported catching good-sized bream and crappie. One angler, fishing from a kayak in one of the lake’s coves, reported catching a 10- to 12-inch crappie using minnows. Minnows still seem to be the preferred bait of choice for crappie, though anglers have said they have had luck with various artificial baits. Bass and catfish have not been reported being caught in large numbers as of yet.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text: Clarity in oxbows, will vary widely from mud lines pushing into the oxbows and heavy stained to fair visibility from 5-15 inches, and we observed around 1-2 feet visibility in a few protected areas like McGuire Oxbow, away from river current Largemouth Bass have improved over the past week. Several large female bass between 6-9 lbs. each have recently been caught. Bass Assassin Shads, plastic lizards, Brush Hogs, tubes and spinnerbaits will draw a reaction in 2-6 feet of water. Bill Lewis crankbaits like the MR-6, and Echo 1.75, and SB-57 MDJ crankbaits were all getting random reaction bites over the past couple weeks from these active roaming Bass in deeper sections of creek channels or…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River fishing report
reports.text: The University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff Bass Fishing Team had no report this week, but its most recent report noted the water temperature was in the mid-60s, about where it has been for a few weeks. Black bass were biting fairly well recently on bladed jigs, spinnerbaits, shallow-diving crankbaits, lipless crankbaits and creature baits/jigs around typical prespawn rocky banks and wooden cover. Some bass were positioned along the first sand drops away from spawning areas.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River (Little Rock Area Pools) fishing report
reports.text:
Fish ’N Stuff (501-834-5733) said the fishing is “really, really good” for bass. Bass are mostly being caught on black and blue jigs and also a Texas-rigged creature in Junebug or black/blue colors. Also, bass have been hitting a bluegill-colored frog in the early morning or early evenings as well as midday if it’s cloudy.
Crappie have been hit or miss with the changing river flow. Most crappie are being caught between the main river and backwaters on a black/chartreuse or white/chartreuse crappie jig. The water level has been fluctuating, which slows the bite (though it does not bother the bass bite now).

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Columbia fishing report
reports.text: Lake Erling Guide Service (870-904-8546) near here said they heard reports that anglers were catching a lot of bass last week, and crappie were biting in about 12 feet of water.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Erling fishing report
reports.text: Lake Erling Guide Service (870-904-8546) said crappie are biting “really good. No reports on bass.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayetteville fishing report
reports.text: Lake Fayetteville Boat Dock (479-444-3476) says anglers catching a lot of crappie and white bass. The crappie catches are still “pretty little.”

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Overcup fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are in the shallow water trying to spawn. Catfish are being caught on yo-yos and trotlines baited with bass minnows. Crappie are still being caught but they are still moving around, and some males are in shallow water.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Poinsett fishing report
reports.text:
Numerous anglers have reported catching good-sized bream and crappie. One angler, fishing from a kayak in one of the lake’s coves, reported catching a 10- to 12-inch crappie using minnows. Minnows still seem to be the preferred bait of choice for crappie, though anglers have said they have had luck with various artificial baits. Bass and catfish have not been reported being caught in large numbers as of yet.
Remember that by state regulation, and while Lake Poinsett continues to grown its forage and predate populations from its 3-year renovation in recent years, bass and crappie are catch-and-release only.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Little Maumelle River fishing report
reports.text:
The bass are going nuts.”
Bass, both spotted bass and largemouths, are biting spinnerbaits, crankbaits, worms, “about anything you throw out there.” Anglers are catching more Kentucky bass (spots) than largemouths, which have been mostly small of late, he said.
Crappie are so-so. Anglers are catching a few in about 3 feet of water, but the crappie do not appear to have moved shallower on the nests, Ray said.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River (Little Rock Area Pools) fishing report
reports.text: Fish ’N Stuff (501-834-5733) said bass fishing is “pretty good” in the backwaters with fish biting in 2-4 feet. Moving further into the main lake, bass are biting on darker colored crankbaits (black or black/chartreuse) in about 6-8 feet off the jetties.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie will be moving into spawning areas as are all the black bass.
Crappie are still scattered from 12-15 feet of water to right up on banks.
Bass and crappie should hit the banks one to two weeks and we hope the weather will stay stable and we can pull off a good spawn.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bull Shoals Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Bass are in prespawn, and overall the bass fishing has been good and everyone is starting to catch them. If it’s flat and sunny, fish swings, points and secondary points with a Jewel Peewee Jig in green pumpkin with either Bass Whacker or Touchdown in orange or blue.
(updated 4-4-2024) Crappie 101 Guide Service reports that crappie are starting to stage on shallower brush piles and structure. Minnows have been working as well as crappie jigs with small fry baits like the Tater Baits.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cane Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Also late last week, anglers on the shoreline reported using worms and minnows for crappie. On Saturday, there was angler use from a boat on the north side of the lake, with minnows attracting both bass and crappie. Also, worms and minnows were being used in other spots for crappie, as well as bream with crickets and worms.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir fishing report
reports.text:
Bates Field and Stream (501-470-1846) said catfish and crappie are still going strong. Crappie are hitting strong on minnows and jigs both. The big crappie are really starting to bite now.
Bass are biting well on plastic crawdads.
The pond is more than 60 acres and has bass, crappie, bream and some winter-stocked rainbow trout.
reports.lake: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text:
For crappie, anglers will find some roaming around chewing while others will be doing the same in pole timber or in brush piles.
Black bass are good super shallow out to 50 feet in guts, main lake points or secondary points, and are biting on Alabama rigs, Carolina rigs, jerkbaits, football heads or crankbaits and Texas-rigged lizards. Stay around the shad and or spawning areas. Some bass are now eating topwater baits as well.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Harris Brake Lake Resort (501-889-2745) says 38-pound buffalo on crappie minnow.
Also anglers are catching crappie just past an island on the lake, including some hitting 14 inches.
Bass minnows are working for them on trotlines.
Bass are doing well, too. A neighbor near the bait shop caught several bass, keeping a limit of 10.
A black bass tournament is scheduled for this Saturday.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayetteville fishing report
reports.text:
The crappie, bream and bass all have been biting well. Crappie appear to be getting a little size on them now, and they are biting jigs more than minnows.
Black bass are biting well on plastics with fish over 2 pounds consistently being caught.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Maumelle fishing report
reports.text:
Fish ’N Stuff (501-834-5733) in Sherwood reports that crappie are spawning and anglers can catch them around the brush piles in 10 feet of water. Try a one-eighth-ounce jighead with a white and chartreuse Crappie Magnet.
(updated 4-4-2024) WestRock Landing in Roland (501-658-5598) reported that the wind has been whipping around the lake this week, slowing some of the fishing, but anglers were catching a bunch of bass on Thursday. For the past week, the largemouth bass bite has been fair. The bass were in prespawn and starting to spawn, and could be found in 2-8 feet of water, while some are being found in deeper areas. Alabama rigs, crankbaits and swimbaits, and pull out that jerkbait to…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ouachita fishing report
reports.text:
Todd Gadberry at Mountain Harbor Resort and Spa (870-867-2191/800-832-2276 out-of-state) said black bass are still very good.
Crappie have slowed a bit, but are biting fair. These fish can still be targeted on shallow structure with minnows or small jigs. Jugs and trotlines are still producing quality catfish catches over main lake points with live or cut bait. The water temperature has creeped back up to range between 55-60 degrees and the clarity is clearing across the lake. The water level Wednesday was a little more than a foot below level pool, at 576.88 feet msl. Call the Mountain Harbor fishing guides (Mike Wurm, 501-622-7717, or Chris Darby, 870-867-7822) for more information…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Little Maumelle River fishing report
reports.text:
Black bass are right up on the bank and in the middle of spawning.
A lot of crappie are also in about that 2-foot range of water now and in the middle of their spawn, too, though some other crappie have been caught deep. The crappie being caught appear to be good-sized now, he added.
Ray said he had nothing to report on bream; he said regular anglers only begin targeting the bream after this spring activity of bass and crappie slows down.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text:
* Largemouth bass’ activity has improved over the past week. Bass Assassin Shads (5-inch size), plastic lizards, Brush Hogs, tubes and spinnerbaits will draw a reaction in 2-6 feet depths. Bill Lewis Crankbaits like the MR-6, and Echo 1.75, and SB-57 MDJ crankbaits were all getting random reaction bites over the past couple of weeks from these active roaming bass in the deeper sections of creek channels or drops from the flats into 8-12 feet structure with stumps present. “We caught good numbers of males and females from 3-6 pounds each over the past two weeks on the 5-inch Bass Assassin Shads, lizards and spinnerbaits in the shallow lily pads, grass and buckbrush.”
The largemouths reaction…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Norfork Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Several large crappie, bass and carp have moved in under Blackburn’s Dock and that is a good sign. The larger crappie want to spawn badly and the males have started to stage back in the creeks.
White bass fishing is picking up but black bass fishing is the best, and several walleye are being caught after moving downstream from the river spawn.”

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Peckerwood Lake fishing report
reports.text:
The crappie are biting both on poles and on the yo-yos. Crappie are moving up into the bushes and tree lines, making it conducive for the folks setting yo-yos with minnows.
Black bass are good; like the crappie, the yo-yos hung around the tree line and bushes are catching some.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Dardanelle fishing report
reports.text: Seth Boone, superintendent at Lake Dardanelle State Park ( 479-890-7474), reported that Lake Dardanelle looks to be entering the spring season strongly with white bass and crappie biting well on live bait such as minnows. Anglers haven’t shared much on the black bass, but catfish seem to be doing OK on chicken liver close to sunset or early evening.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Peckerwood Lake fishing report
reports.text:
THe crappie are biting both on poles and on the yo-yos. Crappie are moving up into the bushes and treelines, making it conducive for the folks setting yo-yos with minnows.
Black bass are good; like the crappie, the yo-yos hung around the treeline and bushes are catching some.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River (Little Rock Area Pools) fishing report
reports.text: Fish ’N Stuff (501-834-5733) reports a lot of anglers say most of the bass they’re catching are through flipping shallow in the backwaters.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are really trying to commit to the spawn; unfortunately the Corps is dropping the lake just at the right time to make the fish pull back some. Black bass are prespawn and are close to the spawn.
Monday and Tuesday, the crappie fishing was good for reporting anglers.
Black bass have been about the same as crappie, they say.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are a little slow. Their guess is that the crappie may be off in the flats. Bass are also up on the shoreline.
They’re liking nightcrawlers and dip baits along with trotline minnows, as well as bass minnows used on the yo-yos.
reports.lake: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are everywhere – up shallow, out roaming and deep on structure. Black bass are pretty much the same as the crappie; use spinnerbaits, topwater lures, crankbaits, Alabama rigs, drop-shots, Carolina rigs,Texas rigs, spoons – a lot is going on every day, some are still spawning, a big shad spawn is going on in different places, and with weather forecasts it looks like the same all next month as well.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Harris Brake Lake Resort (501-889-2745) says crappie are still slow, not what they expect there for this time of year. A few caught some black bass on the bank. Also, some people have caught a few catfish on trotlines and noodles baited with either bass minnows or baby bream.
Black bass are doing well.
Crappie are biting and typical for all this changing water with the weather, so move around from shallow to deep water and good luck. The best colors are silver/chartreuse, Monkey Milk, black/chartreuse, Cajun Cricket, Kiwi, Mo-Glo, silver/Blue Ice, orange/white, Diamond Mist Crappie Magnet, along with minnows and nightcrawlers.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text:
Shelly Jeffrey at Lake Charles State Park (870-878-6595) said bream and crappie continue to bite well this past week, but catfish went into hiding, or no one was looking, and bass or bass anglers are a no-show too.
Crappie are found in shallow water and are good on minnows and jigs. Focus on brush piles, stumps and rocky points. Bream have going the crappie in shallow water, around the brush piles, stumps and rocky points. They prefer worms and crickets, but will also go for jigs. She’s had no reports on bass for a while, and after biting well the previous week, there were no reports on catfish. reports.text:
Black bass are still doing pretty well on spinnerbaits, creature baits, Chatterbaits, crankbaits. Crappie are picky with the bite here and there on jigs and minnows.

reports.text:

On that end, bass anglers are fishing the rivers and the guys who have been doing well have been throwing spinnerbaits around trees or using a finesse jig around trees and laydowns.

reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text:

Catfish anglers are using skipjack, bass minnows and some anglers from the bank are tempting the cats with nightcrawlers.
That still isn’t helping the crappie anglers, who were having good success up until this week.
Bass are biting well. Crappie are biting…

Crappie are related to the brush piles, the stumps and rocky points.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text:
* The largemouth bass activities have been slowly getting better each week. Numerous male bass and a few fat prespawn females, continue to be found roaming flats from 2-6 feet deep where bedding areas exist, searching out new bedding sites. For the last several weeks, these roaming largemouths have been quick to strike on lizards, Brazalo Spinnerbaits, Chatterbaits, Trick Worms, Senkos, salty rat tails and Bass Assassin Shads. A recent bass tournament yielded several good strings of bass for 35-42 pounds, including several in the 7- to 10-pound class of largemouths.
“The shallow-cruising male largemouth bass we found roaming bedding areas over the past couple weeks were around 2.5-3 pounds…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Norfork Lake fishing report
reports.text:
The walleye, stripers and white bass have finished spawning and the crappie are ready and the black bass are not far behind. The spring topwater bite is beginning and the bass and stripers are coming up early after warm nights but not after cold ones. Surprisingly, some crappie and walleye are coming up with them. The male crappie are moving up in the creeks to make nests and the big females are still prespawn feeding, as are the female bass. “I am seeing no bass on the beds yet, but the water has been cloudy until just recently in the creeks.”
The fun part of this area was that the largemouth, spotted and white bass were all feeding heavily on the surface.
As stated above, the bass are…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Buffalo National River/Crooked Creek fishing report
reports.text: With warmer temperatures, the smallmouths could soon become active.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hamilton fishing report
reports.text:
Bass have already started the spawning process, and many small “bucks” (males) have been caught just inside main lake points under trash, pollen sludge, submerged grass and docks. It is very effective at getting in tight places that bass like hide during the spawn.
No catfish or crappie reports.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Maumelle fishing report
reports.text:
Fish ’N Stuff (501-834-5733) said bass are good between 2-6 feet of water.
Largemouth bass are good. Some reports of the bass being found inside the grass 4-12 feet early in the morning and going deep after the sun comes out (scattered at all depths). Kentucky bass ( spotted bass ) are fair. Crappie are good.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River fishing report
reports.text: The University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff Bass Fishing Team said water temperature is in the upper 50s on the main channel of the river, low 60s in Lake Langhofer, and mid- to upper 60s in protected backwaters. Black bass are in all stage of spawn (pre-, active and post-) depending on where you fish.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Crown Lake fishing report
reports.text: The only reports they’ve heard on the lake have come from bass anglers, who report good catches.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: DeGray Lake fishing report
reports.text: Darryl Morris of Family Fishing Trips (501-844-5418) said the crappie and bass are spawning.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: White Oak Lake Area fishing report
reports.text: Angler and guide Stephen Tyson Jr. reported on his Facebook page recently his new personal best black bass catch of White Oak Lake, a fish that topped 11 pounds.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River (Little Rock Area Pools) fishing report
reports.text:
Bass are good off the main river behind jetties or entrances to backwaters on white/chartreuse spinnerbaits, chartreuse/black square-bill Bandit 100 or 200 series; also in the backwaters flipping around grass or wood with a black/blue jig or black/blue Texas-rigged creature bait, and black buzzbait.
Crappie have been very consistent on white/chartreuse, black/chartreuse and red/chartreuse jigs in 3-7 feet of water around any wood.
(updated 4-29-2021) Zimmerman’s Exxon (501-944-2527) said crappie are excellent on the river below both dams and in the backwaters in 4-6 feet depth on black/chartreuse and white/chartreuse Slab Buster Jigs.
“We have customers catching crappie very shallow and…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text:
The crappie bite was going really well, but the last few days it has been a grind. Bass have been pre-spawn/close to spawning.
Crappie are good and being caught around brushpiles and stumps with minnows and jigs. Black bass are good for anglers throwing plastic worms.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cane Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Sarah Reap, assistant superintendent at Cane Creek State Park, said that with the storms last week, activity has been down, especially for crappie. Bass and catfish have remained steady. Bass are still being found regularly around structures, and catfish have continued to be caught with attractants.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are improved after a slight dip in the action. Crappie are on the beds and the bite is good on minnows and jigs. Black bass are biting better with good results this week.
reports.lake: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Crown Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is fair on minnows and jigs. Bass fishing is good; use Senkos or stick worms.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are in all three phases of spawn, and that will continue for a while; they are super shallow out to 20 feet. Black bass are everywhere, super shallow out to 30 feet.
Bass are “really good” in shallow water, 4-5 feet deep around buckbrush, on peanut butter and jelly or green pumpkin jigs, a Texas-rigged green pumpkin creature bait, a shaky head in watermelon color, or a Carolina rig in 15 feet of water, and if there is wind use spinnerbaits or topwater lures. Crappie are good around 7-10 feet around bushes; they’ll bite a Road Runner with a small swimbait on it (white or natural shad colors).

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie continue to bite well but remain in the deeper water. Black bass are good and are being caught around the shoreline. Plastic worms are working, and bass are also biting trotlines baited with bass minnows. Bass minnows, goldfish and perch all are working on trotlines.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Horseshoe Lake fishing report
reports.text:
The crappie are finishing up the spawn.
Bass are moving shallow “and I would assume are getting ready to spawn if they are not doing so now,” Kent says. The ones caught were caught on ⅛-ounce crappie jigs so maybe minnow imitating baits for the bass fishermen will work as well as spinnerbaits.”

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows and jigs, and they were found in their usual haunts around brushpiles and stumps and on rocky points. Bass catching appeared good, but Shelly didn’t get a lead on baits used.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayetteville fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows and jigs. Black bass picked up in the past week with good results.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text: * Largemouth bass: Most of the largemouths up Little River in the oxbows are post-spawn, even though a few straggling female bass still are in spawning mode, and fish are scattered. Brazalo Spinnerbaits in Millwood Mayhem Bream, River Shad and Spot Remover continue catching roaming bass from 2-3 pounds each on flats and creek channel swings from 3-8 feet deep. Chatterbaits in Sexy Shad or bream patterns – using a thumping Bass Assassin Boss Shiner 4.5-inch swimbait trailer in Bluegill Flash, Mama’s 14k or Chico’s Red Ear – picked up a few healthy 3-4 pound largemouths this week. Bass continue randomly roaming shallow on full sun and bright skies in 3-6 feet depth of flats adjacent to deeper…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Beaverfork fishing report
reports.text: Water temperature is around 64 degrees and the crappie spawn in progress; it was delayed. Bass were hitting everything in the box in the shallows, plasting worms and chatterbaits. Crappie are picking up a LOT better, use plastics or jigs, and minnows.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Little Maumelle River fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good around the banks on minnows or jigs. Black bass are being caught around the banks on spinnerbaits in good numbers.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River fishing report
reports.text: The University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff Bass Fishing Team said water temperature is in the mid- to upper 60s. Black bass are biting well on shad-colored crankbaits and blade baits around wind-blown rock and woody cover.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River (Little Rock Area Pools) fishing report
reports.text:
Bass are good on black/blue jigs, Texas rigs and creature baits fished around the jetties. Crappie are good in the entrances to back waters and around the jetties in 7-8 feet depth on orange/chartreuse, blue/chartreuse and black/chartreuse crappie jigs.
(updated 4-15-2021) Zimmerman’s Exxon (501-944-2527) said crappie are excellent below the Terry Lock and Dam.
He reports that the flow was greatly reduced and bass could be found in less than 3 feet of water out of the current.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text:
“The spawn was starting to happen and now the crappie are pulling back out. Same thing with the bass and it really squashed an up-and-coming striper bite.
I have seen this before and if the conditions do not return favorable soon, I am afraid the crappie may just reabsorb their eggs. It happened last year to some extent as I was catching crappie mid-May with brown nonviable eggs in them.
Bass, same deal, they were staged and I am sure they are pulling back out.
Crappie are good and being caught in 8-12 feet depth on minnows and jigs. Black bass are good in that same 8-12 feet range and biting spinnerbaits, crankbaits and Wiggle Warts.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cane Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: There are reports of people catching bass, bream, crappie and catfish from this past week. Bass are being found around structure, catfish with attractant baits, reports of bream being caught on trotlines with minnows, and crappie with minnows and jigs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Clear Lake fishing report
reports.text: McSwain Sports Center (501-945-2471) said crappie are good on minnows and jigs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are just fair, as the cold snap has delayed the crappie spawn, they say. Black bass are fair.
reports.lake: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text:
The crappie fishing is still going good all over, from 6 inches out to 20 feet of water on minnows, jigs and crankbaits. Black bass are shallow for the most part or headed that way or headed back out deep eating everything in your tackle boxes; get out and get them while you have them hemmed up in shallow water.
Bass are good. Anglers will also find a good bite from suspended bass on a single swimbait. As for crappie, some people are catching them in treetops in 10-15 feet of water, or up shallow around the bushes, on jigs in Tennessee Shad, Popsicle and Electric Chicken colors. Also, crappie catches were coming on a Crappie Magnet in natural color or salt and pepper color.
At left, Tom…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are still in deeper water but the bite remains good. Black bass are good and have moved up around the shoreline; fish with a green pumpkin or watermelon plastic worm for best results, as well as bass minnows. Bass minnows, goldfish and baby bream are working on the trotlines.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Horseshoe Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Kent Williams of Oxbow Guide Service (870-278-7978) says there are crappie on the beds.
Bass are shallow. Several baits are working to catch bass right now. Some bass are still showing up for crappie fishermen.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Catherine (Below Carpenter Dam) fishing report
reports.text: The crappie spawn has gotten off to a slow start this season, but small catches have been reported with the best results during periods of generation. The white bass and crappie are crowded close together in the tailrace with both species caught over sandbars and rock structure.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows, jigs and worms. Bass are fair, with spinnerbaits and plastic worms working best.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayetteville fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows and jigs. Black bass are a little slow now, but anglers had fair results; crankbaits are your best bet.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Maumelle fishing report
reports.text:
WestRock Landing in Roland (501-658-5598) said there have not been many reports on the white bass or crappie in the last few days. The largemouth bass bite is good. Tuesday night’s tournament saw the team of Dustin Crow and Matt France haul in five bass worth 12.76 pounds, while Frank Ramey and Doug Rich caught the Big Bass of 4.14 pounds and had 11.09 pounds total on the stringer. The Kentucky/spotted bass bite is fair. Reports of the white bass being found mixed in with the crappie. Crappie are fair with no reports in recent days.
On May 1, Lake Maumelle will play host to the first Bit’s Big Bass Tournament. The two-person fishing tournament has a five-fish limit, and a qualifying bass…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Overcup fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are good in the early mornings, with the bite found close to the shoreline. Crappie are biting at trotlines. Bass are good, mainly in the Caney Creek area, on a variety of baits.
Bass are doing well on plastic worms and spinnerbaits around the buckbrush. Crappie are slow but still catching some good ones in brushtops and spider-rigging.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Poinsett fishing report
reports.text: Fathead minnows, golden shiners, threadfin shad and bluegill have been added to the lake to build up a huge food supply for bass, catfish and other sportfish that will be added next year to give the lake a jump start after its recent renovation.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text: * Largemouth bass: Most bass up Little River in the oxbows are post-spawn, although main lake pockets continue in varying degrees of pre- and post-spawning conditions for the past few weeks on Millwood. Most of the oxbows up and along Little River continue seeing post-spawn largemouths and pre-spawn crappie. Brazalo Spinnerbaits in Millwood Mayhem Bream, River Shad and Spot Remover continue catching solid bass from 2-4 pounds each, over the past several weeks, and Chatterbaits in Sexy Shad or Bream patterns, continue to pick up a few healthy 3-4 pound largemouths this week. Bass continue randomly roaming shallow on full sun and bright skies in the 3-6 foot depths of flats adjacent to deeper…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: War Eagle/White River fishing report
reports.text: The smallmouth bass fishing is excellent, and females may have eggs still, so it would be good to catch and then release them.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Maumelle fishing report
reports.text:
WestRock Landing in Roland (501-658-5598) said there have not been many reports on the white bass or crappie in recent days. The largemouth bass bite is good. Tuesday night’s tournament saw the team of Dustin Crow and Matt France haul in five bass worth 12.76 pounds, while Frank Ramey and Doug Rich caught the Big Bass of 4.14 pounds and had 11.09 pounds total on the stringer. The Kentucky/spotted bass bite is fair. Reports of the white bass being found mixed in with the crappie. Crappie are fair with no reports in recent days.
On Saturday, May 1, Lake Maumelle will play host to the inaugural Bit’s Big Bass Tournament. The two-person fishing tournament has a five-fish limit, and a qualifying…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nimrod fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are excellent. Black bass are good.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Overcup fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are good in the early mornings, with the bite found close to the shoreline. Crappie are biting at trotlines. Bass are good, mainly in the Caney Creek area, on a variety of baits.
Bass are slow but anglers are still catching some with June bugs and watermelon plastic worms. Crappie are doing fair on yo-yos at night on minnows.
Crappie are good (David tells us that “the dogwood is blooming so crappie are spawning”). Black bass are good.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Atkins fishing report
reports.text: Crappie have moved back deep and are biting fair using minnows or a Bobby Garland Jig in chartreuse or bone white colors. Black bass are fair and also are deep this week; best bet is a plastic worm in watermelon seed or green pumpkin color.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: War Eagle/White River fishing report
reports.text: The smallmouth bass fishing is excellent, and females may still have eggs, so it would be wise to catch and then release them.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ouachita fishing report
reports.text:
At left, Donna Currington caught several nice crappie on Lake Ouachita on April 11.
Darryl Morris of Family Fishing Trips Guide Service (501-844-5418) said he has been fishing both Ouachita and DeGray Lake, and he’s find a similar pattern: The crappie are great on jigs and minnows on staging brushpiles fished 8 feet deep. The cooler mornings haven’t slowed the crappie.
(updated 4-22-2021) Todd Gadberry at Mountain Harbor Resort and Spa (870-867-2191/800-832-2276 out of state) reports that black bass are very good. Crappie are good.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River (Little Rock Area Pools) fishing report
reports.text:
Bass reports are good in that a lot of fish are being caught.
Crappie are good on orange/chartreuse and pink/chartreuse crappie jigs fished behind the jetties in 4-8 feet of water.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are good and getting better daily. Bass are staging.
Crappie are fair and are being found in 6-15 feet depth. Black bass appear to be in pre-spawn mode.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bull Shoals Lake fishing report
reports.text: Some small Kentucky bass are trying but the major drops have them holding.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cane Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie continues to be caught on minnows and jigs. Bass are still being found around structures, and catfish are being caught on trotlines and limblines with large minnows and attractant baits.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir fishing report
reports.text: Crappie and edging to spawning. Black bass are on the move to shallow water.
reports.lake: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie continue to be caught at will on jigs, minnows and crankbaits all over the lake and rivers at various depths, from super shallow out to 25 feet. Black bass are on beds and hanging out to 35 feet and can be caught on crankbaits, plastics, Alabama rigs, jerkbaits, spinnerbaits and jigs.
Bass are good. Deeper bass in the 10-15 feet range can be caught on Carolina rigs and crankbaits. Crappie are good, though a little sporadic, around the bushes with Road Runners working well.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are still deep but they are biting well. Black bass are good; try crankbaits or topwater baits. They’re biting nightcrawlers, glow worms, bass minnows and are being caught on trotlines close to shore.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Horseshoe Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Kent Williams of Oxbow Guide Service (870-278-7978) says crappie are still scattered.
Male black bass are showing up in the shallows with several reports of bass being caught by crappie fishermen searching for spawning crappie.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Atkins fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair using minnows or Bobby Garland jigs. Black bass are fair; try green pumpkin worms for best chances.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text: Shelly Jeffrey at Lake Charles State Park (870-878-6595) said there were reports of crappie biting this week amid high water, but not a lot else was reported. Crappie are good on minnows, jigs and worms. The crappie are up around the brushpiles, stumps and close to rocky points. Nothing heard on black bass or bream.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayetteville fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows and jigs. Black bass are fair; crankbaits, jerkbaits, bass minnows and jigs worked best.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nimrod fishing report
reports.text: Crappie appear about a week out from spawning and are on the shoreline in the brush. Black bass are good.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Overcup fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are good on the shoreline, hitting minnows and jigs. Bass are good on a variety of baits.
Bass are slow but should be picking up. Crappie are starting to move into the shoreline in 2 feet of water. Johnny says, “I caught several crappie around 3.2 pounds and 3.1 pounds, and a 38-pound flathead the other day.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text: * Largemouth bass: Bass have been in varying degrees of annual spawning mode for the past 4-6 weeks on Millwood. Most of the oxbows up and along Little River are seeing post-spawn largemouths and pre-spawn crappie. Brazalo Spinnerbaits in white/chartreuse, Millwood Mayhem Bream and Spot Remover continue catching decent bass from 2-5 pounds each over the past 2 weeks, and Chatterbaits continue to pick up a few healthy 3- to 4-pound largemouths this week. “Most bass we are finding continue randomly roaming shallow on full sun and bright skies in the 3-6 foot depths of flats adjacent to deeper drops into 7-10 feet depth ranges,” Siefert says. Anywhere a creek channel runs near spawning flats…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Peckerwood Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows and jigs. Black bass are good on jigs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Upper White Oak Lake fishing report
reports.text:
AGFC Fisheries staff and biologists electrofished the lake for largemouth bass in recent weeks. The bass collected in the upper lake were in excellent condition and appear to have been feeding well during the drawdown.
(updated 4-15-2021) AGFC Fisheries staff and biologists electrofished the lake for largemouth bass during March and April. Staff also saw plenty of large bass, including a 9-pounder and several 6-7 pounders.
(updated 4-15-2021) AGFC Fisheries staff and biologists electrofished the lake for largemouth bass during March and April. the bass fishery appears to be doing well, according to biologists. Also, many of the bass were collected near patches of vegetation among the…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Brewer Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good (David tells us that “the dogwood is blooming so crappie are spawning”). Black bass are good.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Crown Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie appear to be moving closer to the shoreline. The black bass bite is good, just in time for a tournament planned for Crown Lake on Saturday (April 17).

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hamilton fishing report
reports.text:
THE BASS SPAWN IS ON! Bass have moved up hot and heavy into shallow areas and creek channels doing their thing. Please be respectful and put big Mama back so we can have more good bass fishing for years to come.
Bream and crappie are biting well on deeper docks and shallow, submerged brush all over the lake.
Darryl Morris of Family Fishing Trips Guide Service (501-844-5418) said the crappie are working the spawn just like the black bass.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Little Maumelle River fishing report
reports.text: Crappie, however, continue to bite well. Black bass are around the bank and in shallow water.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bear Creek Lake/Storm Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Tyler Ball, park ranger at Mississippi River State Park (870-295-4040), said anglers report catching a few largemouth bass with artificial baits and minnows at Bear Creek Lake. Some of these bass were reported to still be full of eggs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hamilton fishing report
reports.text:
THE BASS SPAWN IS ON! Bass have moved up hot and heavy into shallow areas and creek channels doing their thing. Please be respectful and put big Mama back so we can have more good bass fishing for years to come.
Bream and crappie are biting well on deeper docks and shallow, submerged brush all over the lake.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Norfork Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie and bass have both started their spawning process, which will continue for several weeks if not more.
Crappie are being caught with three different methods. The crappie have typically been on the tops of the brush or out along the sides of the brush. Let it fall slowly and typically a crappie will pick it up before it stops falling. There are schools of crappie out in the deep water staging for the spawn and when your bait goes through the school it gets hammered.
Bass fishing has also been very good. The bass are up in shallow water feeding on baitfish and small bluegills. “I have found them back in creeks and coves. A lot of the time they are all the way in the back in very…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Spring River fishing report
reports.text: For spin-fishers, trout cranks and Flicker Shad are working well on the bass, and hot pink, red and white Trout Magnets are working well for the trout.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: DeGray Lake fishing report
reports.text:
“Crappie fishing has been pretty good all around.
Darryl Morris of Family Fishing Trips Guide Service (501-844-5418) said that as he also found at Lake Ouachita (see below), crappie fishing is going great at this time. Males are bedding and females are staging, meaning he and his guests have caught crappie on both minnows and jigs as shallow as 3 feet and as deep as 12 feet.
(update 4-15-2021) Local crappie angler Charles Abernathy says, “I got a chance to get on the water for a couple of hours before dark (Wednesday).

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Columbia fishing report
reports.text: AGFC biologists and staff electrofished the lake in March and April to study the largemouth bass population. Nearly one out of every three fish was over 16 inches long, and 5 percent of the bass collected were longer than 20 inches.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Erling fishing report
reports.text: AGFC biologists and staff electrofished the lake in March and April to study the largemouth bass population. Lake Erling is the top-ranked bass fishery in Arkansas over the past five years (2016-2020), according to the results from angler-submitted Arkansas Tournament Information Program data.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake June fishing report
reports.text: AGFC biologists and staff electrofished the lake in March and April to study the largemouth bass population. The largemouth bass population appears healthy and is right on track with what biologists expect to see following a lake renovation. A large majority of the bass sampled were from the initial stocking and about 10-14 inches long. Additionally, biologists also saw high numbers of quality-sized bream and crappie.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River fishing report
reports.text:
Bass are good on black/blue Chatterbait, chartreuse/black crankbaits, a black/blue jig, and white/chartreuse spinnerbaits just off the main river and in the backwaters. Crappie are good in 4-5 feet of water behind some of the jetties on orange/chartreuse, white/chartreuse and blue/chartreuse crappie jigs.
The shallow water bite is good for bass and crappie.
(updated 4-1-2021) Zimmerman’s Exxon (501-944-2527) said crappie are excellent below the Terry Lock and Dam and Murray Lock and Dam on crappie petit minnows.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text:
“ Bass are pre-spawn hitting stick baits and cranks. Crappie are on the move to the banks. Crappie fishing is good and getting better with time. Been catching some big ones jigging for crappie. Next few weeks look for bass and crappie to be in beds.
Crappie are good; fish minnows or jigs around the brushpiles. Black bass are being caught in shallow water and the bite is good.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Brewer Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are still in deeper water but the bite is good. Black bass are biting well. The bass are closer to the shoreline in the weeds.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cane Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is on right now. Reports are coming in that they can be found at a depth of around 2-3 feet and are being caught on minnows and crappie jigs. Bass are falling into a spring pattern and can be found fishing around structure.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie still show signs of being or beginning to get into spawn mode. Black bass are good in the shallow water now.
(updated 3-25-2021) Hatchet Jack’s Sports Shop in Crystal Hill off I-40 (758-4958) reports that crappie are “really good” off the Highway 89 bridge.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Crown Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows and jigs. The crappie are around the brushpiles. Bass are good on crankbaits and jerkbaits.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Dierks Lake fishing report
reports.text: Local angler Charles Abernathy made a stopover this past week at Dierks and says big crappie are biting well there.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are eating all over. Black bass are scattered all over, top to bottom, shallow to deep out to 60 feet.
Bass are good on spinnerbaits, jerkbaits, floating worms fished around the bushes, Texas-rigged lizards and Carolina rigs in 10-15 feet of water off secondary points. Crappie are good on Road Runners with grubs swimming around the bushes in 5-6 feet water (fish a natural shad pattern, pink/chartreuse or white/chartreuse colors).

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are still mostly being found in deeper water, while the bite remains good. Black bass are good. Good results were had with goldfish, bass minnows and dough bait.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text: Shelly Jeffrey at Lake Charles State Park (870-878-6595) said that while crappie is typically the target here, it’s black bass and catfish that were biting the best the past week. Bass were good for anglers using crankbaits or plastic works. They were finding bass around the brush and rocky points. Crappie were not reported, and neither were bream.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayetteville fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows and jigs. Black bass are good using crankbaits, jerkbaits, minnows and jigs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hamilton fishing report
reports.text:
Largemouth and spotted bass are feeding aggressively in the shallow areas that lead into pockets of the lakes. Bass are smashing several types of baits but the main focus is on a bubblegum floating Trick Worm and a jig like the Slycked Back Rowdy Ravager and Copper Crawler, AKA Copper colored and green and brown.
Bream are smoking hot right now along with crappie in 10-20 feet of water over and on submerged brush. Hybrids are scattered everywhere the bream and bass are, so don’t get too focused on one species.
Darryl Morris of Family Fishing Trips Guide Service (501-844-5418) said the crappie are working the spawn just like the black bass.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nimrod fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are very shallow now, about 2-3 feet depth on the shoreline. Black bass are good on spinnerbaits (go with white) or Chatterbait.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Overcup fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on the shoreline, hitting minnows and jigs. Bass are good on a variety of baits.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Little Maumelle River fishing report
reports.text: Crappie improved to good this week. Black bass bounced back with good catches.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text: * Largemouth bass: Bass have been in varying degrees of annual spawning mode for three past 3-4 weeks on Millwood. Most of the oxbows up and along Little River are seeing post-spawn largemouths and pre-spawn crappie. Brazalo Spinnerbaits in white/chartreuse, Millwood Mayhem Bream and Spot Remover caught decent bass over the past two weeks, and Chatterbaits again picked up some healthy 3-to 7-pound largemouths this week. “Most bass we are finding continue randomly roaming shallow on full sun and bright skies in the 3-6 foot depths of flats adjacent to deeper drops into 7-10 feet depth ranges,” Siefert says. Anywhere a creek channel runs near spawning flats with vertical structure nearby…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Peckerwood Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on minnows and jigs. Black bass are good on jigs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Spring River fishing report
reports.text: Was slow but caught several smallmouth and a few nice trout.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Dardanelle fishing report
reports.text:
Bass have been on fire with an excellent topwater bite early and late and just before and during the storm fronts.
Crappie have been great and suspended in some places, scattered in other areas. Many crappie this week have been caught on bass lures. Fishing minnows and jigs along the grassy banks and the larger stumps will put crappie in the boat; still, bright colors have been working the best.
Bass are good on white spinnerbaits and white/chartreuse spinners, as well as Jackhammer Chatterbait and black/blue and green pumpkin Senkos in shallow and grassy areas.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Maumelle fishing report
reports.text: WestRock Landing in Roland (501-658-5598) said they have been receiving great reports on crappie this week. And the Lake Maumelle Tuesday Night Bass Tournament season is back up and running, contact WestRock Landing for more information on how to compete in the series. Lee Brizzolari and Wes Lowder hauled in 14.33 pounds worth of bass to win, while Jeremy Cole and Aaron Cole hooked a big bass of 4.37 pounds. The largemouth bass bite is good. The Kentucky/spotted bass bite is fair. The great bite from the crappie is coming in about 2-4 feet of water as the males are shallow on the beds. Other anglers are saying that female crappie can be found moving in at 8-10 feet. Also, reports have come…

reports.title: Arkansas River at Morrilton fishing report
reports.text: He also says that black bass appear to be sitting on top of the jetty. A few bass were caught in about 5 feet of water on top of the jetty in the late evening, he said.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Beaverfork fishing report
reports.text: Water temperature is around 60 degrees and crappie spawn in imminent Bass are hitting everything in the box in the shallows. Crappie are still suspended, but some are being caught using plastics or jigs, and minnows.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Bass are good from Prairie Creek on up into the rivers. Crappie are staged and ready to move up next week or two.
Crappie are good, but the bigger fish are to be found in 5-20 feet depth. Black bass are fair; try spinnerbaits, crankbaits, jigs and jerkbaits.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Brewer Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are still in deeper water but the bite is good. Black bass are biting well. The bass are closer to the shoreline in the weeds.
Crappie and bass both were good along the grass lines.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cane Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie fishing is starting to pick up.
Bass are falling into a spring pattern and can be found fishing around structure.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report

reports.text:
Crappie, they say, are starting to get into spawn mode. Black bass are moving into shallow water and are biting well on spinnerbaits and topwaters.
(updated 3-25-2021) Hatchet Jack’s Sports Shop in Crystal Hill off I-40 (758-4958) reports that crappie are “really good” off the Highway 89 bridge.
